newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles mayor signs $4 bln budget into law.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles mayor signs $4 bln budget into law.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan has signed into law the city's $4 billion spending plan for fiscal 1997-1998 despite initial concerns with one city council budget amendment, his office said Wednesday.

The amendment, approved by the council in May, called for a $1.5 million boost in funding for city council offices. Chris O'Donnell, Riordan's budget director, said at the time that the funding change was "disturbing."
Despite the concern, Riordan decided to sign the amended spending plan into law, ending the city's budget process earlier than expected, his office said.
"He made the determination not to veto it and signed it into law. So it is done," spokeswoman Kristina Parham said.
The mayor's $4 billion spending plan -- $50 million smaller than last year's budget -- contains a reserve of $30 million, and seeks no new taxes.

The mayor's bond proposals -- a $465 million bond for police and fire facilities and a $151 million bond for library improvements -- are not included in the budget pact. They will be reviewed by the city council separately.
